narrative_purpose: Illustrates Hurdle 1 — immune tolerance — by contrasting an intruder being destroyed with a symbiont being accepted, so the reader sees that the same defences can be made to stand down.
subject: Two contrasting scenes side by side against dark tissue: on the left, a small foreign microbe swarmed and torn apart by aggressive angular immune cells firing sharp bright alarm bursts; on the right, a calm symbiotic organism sitting intact inside host tissue while the same immune cells hold back in a quiet ring around it, their alarm bursts dimmed to a soft cool glow, forming a permissive niche.
scene: A left-destruction, right-tolerance comparison of how a host body treats a foreign organism.
camera: A flat comparison view, two scenes of equal size divided by a soft vertical seam.
light: Left scene lit by harsh bright alarm flashes; right scene lit by soft calm cyan glow; both over dark tissue.
palette: Void-indigo tissue base, Pandora cyan and living teal for the calm right scene, a restrained sharp accent for the alarm bursts on the left; the guest a gentle teal.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, observed-from-life confidence, luminous and atmospheric.
detail_level: Crisp on the immune cells and their alarm signals in both scenes; dark tissue background kept simple.
composition: Two equal scenes divided vertically, the destroyed microbe left, the tolerated guest right; dark margins for labels.
consistency_notes: The same kind of immune cell appears in both scenes, aggressive left and quiescent right. Cool palette, alarm accents used sparingly.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no leader lines, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
